title: Georgia Sales Tax Guide: Rates & Compliance
summary: Our Georgia sales tax guide goes over state and local rates, nexus thresholds, how food is taxed, and everything else you need to know to stay compliant.
body_markdown:
## Georgia sales tax at a glance


State taxing authority Georgia Department of Revenue


Georgia sales tax rate 4%


Local tax rates 2% to 5%


Combined sales tax rate range 6% to 9%


Economic nexus threshold $100,000 in gross revenue or 200 transactions


Website[dor.georgia.gov](https://dor.georgia.gov/)


Tax line(877) 423-6711


Georgia has a 4% base sales tax rate, but cities and counties add their own local taxes.


For example, Atlanta pays 8.9%, including 4% state, 3% county, 1.5% city, and a 0.4% special district add-on.


About three dozen jurisdictions statewide, including Muscogee County (Columbus), reach 9%.


This sales tax applies to most tangible goods. Groceries are exempt from the state tax, but local taxes usually still apply.


Georgia sales tax can be confusing since some items are taxed and some are not. For example, prescription drugs are exempt, but clothing isn't.


Sellers can trigger[nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-nexus) in a few ways. Physical presence in Georgia, $100,000 in gross revenue, or 200 separate transactions delivered into the state in the current or prior calendar year trigger nexus.


Once you establish nexus, you must register through the[Georgia Tax Center](https://gtc.dor.ga.gov/) and collect sales tax at the correct destination rate. You will file on the schedule the Department of Revenue gives you.


The real complexity in Georgia isn't the state rate; it's what counties can pile on top of it. Counties can stack several 1% local taxes at once, covering general revenue, capital projects, schools, and transportation. Most are voter-approved for a fixed term, so rates shift every quarter as levies expire or get renewed.

## Georgia sales tax rates and calculations


When you add the 4% state rate to whatever local taxes a county and city have voted in, you land somewhere between 6% and 9% for most GA delivery addresses. Averaged out across the whole state, that works out to[roughly 7.4%.](https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/sales-tax-rates/)


### List of local sales tax rates in Georgia


One challenge in Georgia is that local rates can change quarterly. They also vary by exact address, zip code, and special tax district.


The rates in this table are from[Georgia’s general rate chart](https://dor.georgia.gov/sales-tax-rates-general) for October 1 to December 31, 2026. Check Georgia's current quarterly rate chart before applying anything to an actual sale.


City County Combined Rate


**Atlanta** Fulton 8.9%


**Roswell** Fulton 7.75%


**Sandy Springs** Fulton 7.75%


**Savannah** Chatham 7%


**Augusta** Richmond 9%


**Columbus** Muscogee 9%


**Macon** Bibb 8%


**Decatur** DeKalb 8%


**Marietta** Cobb 6%


**Lawrenceville** Gwinnett 6%


### How to calculate Georgia sales tax


Multiply the taxable sale amount by the combined rate at the delivery address. A $100 sale delivered to an Atlanta address, for example, carries $8.90 in tax since the combined tax rate is 8.9%.


### Origin vs. destination sourcing in Georgia


Georgia uses[destination-based sourcing as opposed to origin-based](https://www.numeral.com/blog/origin-based-vs-destination-based-sales-tax) .


That means the tax is calculated based on where the customer receives the product, which is why something like Atlanta's added city tax depends on the delivery address rather than on where the seller is located.


### Is Georgia a Streamlined Sales Tax State?


Yes, Georgia is a full member of the Streamlined Sales and Use Tax Agreement. Remote sellers can register through the[Streamlined Sales Tax system](https://www.sstregister.org/) and cover Georgia alongside other member states in a single application.


## Sales tax nexus in Georgia


[Nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-nexus) means you have enough connections with a state that the state can require you to collect sales tax on its behalf.


Before 2018, states couldn’t require out-of-state sellers to charge the state sales tax on online purchases. In[South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc.](https://www.numeral.com/blog/south-dakota-v-wayfair) , the U.S. Supreme Court overturned that precedent, and states with a sales tax began setting nexus thresholds.


[Physical and economic nexus rules in Georgia](https://www.numeral.com/nexus/georgia) matter most for most businesses selling into the state.


States each have their own nexus threshold, but generally, a business has[physical nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/physical-nexus) if it has a physical presence in the state, such as an office, warehouse, employees, or inventory.


[Economic nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/economic-nexus) means an out-of-state business meets the dollar or transaction threshold required to charge sales tax to customers in that state.


Nexus Type Threshold


**Physical** Any physical presence in Georgia, including an office, warehouse, employees, or inventory held in a third-party fulfillment center


**Economic** $100,000 in gross revenue or 200 separate retail transactions delivered into Georgia during the current or previous calendar year


**Marketplace**[Marketplace facilitators](https://www.numeral.com/blog/marketplace-facilitator) that exceed Georgia’s economic nexus threshold must collect and remit sales tax on behalf of their third-party sellers


**Click-through** More than $50,000 in Georgia sales during the past 12 months from referrals by in-state affiliates paid on commission


**Affiliate** A related company operating in Georgia under a similar name or product line, regardless of sales volume


**Trade show** A single Georgia trade show appearance of five days or fewer within a 12-month period does not create nexus on its own, provided prior-year Georgia net income was $100,000 or less. Tax is still due on sales made at the show.


### Economic Nexus for Remote Sellers Explained


The $100,000 in gross revenue or 200-transaction thresholds have been in place since January 1, 2020.


However, not every sale counts toward them.


Resale transactions backed by a valid[exemption certificate](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESdQHrOzAVaBzrbzTLuNKo2yEsABOAoCcStGhnU6RGFfCHw1Ntf5m7o7Wg90R9gurqzHuGmrKU9y-XTLANS0hNcFXgtJE5YUO8W6xxEuNzWgTtQRwrum9ObrOBSJbF_Rsz_qnOSiqWPX9tsPQBuNEwP8wsJLlKoA) don’t count, and neither do sales a registered marketplace facilitator already collects on.


Once you reach the threshold, the obligation to collect starts with the next taxable sale.


## What's taxable and exempt in Georgia


Georgia taxes most tangible goods by default. Groceries and prescription drugs get broad exemptions, but clothing does not.[Digital products](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-digital-goods) plus a handful of services run on their own separate rules entirely.


Category Taxable? Notes


**Tangible personal property** Yes Most physical goods are taxable unless specifically exempt


**Groceries** Varies Exempt from the 4% state rate but generally still subject to local sales tax


**Clothing and footwear** Yes No standing exemption; occasional back-to-school holidays require separate legislative approval each year


**Prescription drugs** No Fully exempt


**SaaS** Generally no Treated as a nontaxable service when the customer only accesses provider-hosted software


**Specified digital products** Varies Taxable when the buyer receives a permanent right of use that is not tied to continued payments


**Services** Varies Most services are exempt; a short, enumerated list is taxable


**Shipping** Varies Follows the taxability of the underlying sale


### What's subject to sales tax in Georgia


- Most retail sales of tangible personal property
- Prepared food, alcohol, and dietary supplements, none of which qualify for the grocery exemption
- Specified digital products delivered with a permanent right of use, like downloaded music, movies, e-books, and video games
- A short list of enumerated services, including in-state transportation of individuals and certain repair or installation labor tied to a taxable sale


### What's exempt from sales tax in Georgia


- Groceries and unprepared food are exempt from the state's 4% portion
- Prescription drugs and certain medical devices
- Sales for resale backed by a valid exemption certificate
- Qualifying purchases by nonprofit and government entities


### SaaS and digital goods taxability in Georgia


Georgia distinguishes between a digital product that changes hands for good and software you simply log into.


A specified digital product, think a downloaded book, song, movie, or game, becomes taxable once the buyer gets a permanent right to use it and doesn't have ongoing payments.


Cloud-hosted software usually lands somewhere else entirely.[Georgia treats SaaS as nontaxable](https://www.numeral.com/blog/saas-sales-tax-georgia) when a customer only accesses provider-hosted software and never takes title, possession, or control of it.


### Resale and exemption certificates in Georgia


Businesses buying goods for resale use[Form ST-5](https://dor.georgia.gov/st-5-certificate-exemption) , the Sales and Use Tax Certificate of Exemption, or Form ST-5M for manufacturing purchases.


Out-of-state[resale certificates](https://www.numeral.com/blog/resale-certificates) , the Streamlined Certificate of Exemption, and the[MTC Uniform Sales & Use Tax Resale Certificate](https://www.mtc.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/01/Unif-Resale-Cert-revised-10-14-22.pdf) also work here, as long as the seller is registered in another member state.


Hang onto exemption certificates, such as[resale certificates](https://www.numeral.com/blog/resale-certificates) , along with the sales records behind them, for at least three years.


There's no fixed renewal schedule, but an incomplete or outdated certificate can get tossed out as invalid the moment an audit starts.


## Registering for a Georgia sales tax license


Georgia calls this a Sales and Use Tax Certificate of Registration, issued after a business completes registration online through the[Georgia Tax Center](https://gtc.dor.ga.gov/) . It doesn't expire or require renewal, as long as the business continues under the same ownership and structure.


[Registration](https://www.numeral.com/product/registrations) asks for the legal business name, entity type, FEIN or Social Security number, address, and ownership details. Georgia law also requires the certificate to be displayed at every registered business location, not just the main one.


### Registration requirements for remote sellers


Remote sellers register through that same Georgia Tax Center system once they cross the economic nexus threshold.


Because Georgia is a full Streamlined Sales Tax member, they can also register through the[Streamlined Sales Tax system](https://www.sstregister.org/) to cover multiple member states at once, with collection generally expected to start on the next taxable sale after crossing the line.


## Collecting Georgia Sales Tax


Once you're registered, the work is the same on every sale. Determine whether the item is taxable, apply the rate for the delivery address, collect the tax at checkout, and record it for your return.


### Marketplace sales


When a marketplace facilitator exceeds Georgia's economic nexus threshold, it collects and remits tax on behalf of its third-party sellers.


Sellers still need to track those marketplace sales for their own[nexus tracking](https://www.numeral.com/product/nexus-tracking) , and they're obligated to collect tax on anything sold outside the marketplace, including through their own site.


Storing inventory in a Georgia fulfillment center, including[Amazon FBA warehouses](https://www.numeral.com/blog/amazon-fba-sales-tax) , creates physical nexus on its own. That can mean a marketplace seller needs a Georgia registration even when the platform already handles tax on the facilitated sales.


### Shipping and delivery charges


[Shipping charges](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-shipping) generally follow whatever the underlying sale does. Tax the product, and seller-charged delivery or freight is generally taxable too, even when listed separately on the invoice.


If the underlying sale is untaxed, the delivery charge usually stays untaxed as well.


## Filing and paying Georgia sales tax


Every new registrant starts on a monthly filing schedule, no exceptions, for at least the first six months.


After that stretch, a business can request a change, and the Department of Revenue assigns quarterly or annual filing based on average liability.


Filing Frequency General Requirement


**Monthly** Average state tax liability above $200 per month; this is the default filing frequency for all new registrants


**Quarterly** Average liability of less than $200 per month over six consecutive months, with written approval from the department


**Annual** Average state tax liability under $50 per month for at least six consecutive months


Returns and payments are due on the 20th of the month following the reporting period. Local taxes are included on the same return, so there's no separate local filing to worry about, and zero returns are still required even when nothing sold that period.


Dealers whose prior-year state sales tax liability[topped $60,000](https://dor.georgia.gov/taxes/business-taxes/sales-use-tax/file-pay) must remit a prepaid estimated payment equal to 50% of their estimated liability, calculated from the previous year’s average monthly state tax.


There's also a small reward for staying on time. A vendor's compensation, worth 3% of the first $3,000 in tax due plus 0.5% on anything above that, though it disappears the moment a return is late.


### Filing Georgia sales tax online


Georgia keeps registration, filing, and payment all in one place, the[Georgia Tax Center](https://gtc.dor.ga.gov/) , where businesses file Form ST-3 and pay electronically.


No local jurisdiction runs its own separate system, so a single GTC return covers the state rate and all local add-ons.


[Our guide to filing GA sales tax](https://www.numeral.com/blog/how-to-file-georgia-sales-tax-online) walks through the process step by step.


## Georgia sales tax penalties and interest


If you miss the deadline, Georgia adds a[late filing penalty](https://www.numeral.com/blog/what-happens-if-you-dont-collect-or-remit-sales-tax) of 5% of the tax due, or $5, whichever is greater, for every month or partial month the return sits unfiled, up to a ceiling of 25% or $25. Late payment brings a separate penalty on that same schedule.


Interest piles on top monthly, at the federal prime rate plus 3%, a figure the Department of Revenue resets every January. For 2026, it is 9.75% annually.


If you knowingly file something false or fraudulent, a flat 50% penalty is added on top of everything else.


## Georgia sales tax recordkeeping and audits


Keep sales records, exemption and resale certificates, and returns and payment records on file for at least three years.


The Department of Revenue can[audit](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-audit) a business to verify reported sales, taxability calls, exemptions claimed, rates applied, and whether it collected and remitted the right amount.


If you disagree with an audit, you can follow the[administrative appeals process](https://dor.georgia.gov/protests-and-appeals) . You have 45 days from the date on the proposed assessment to file a protest with the Department.


You can file it online through the Georgia Tax Center or by mailing[Form TSD-1](https://dor.georgia.gov/tsd-1-protest-proposed-assessment-or-refund-denial) with your supporting documentation. If the Department then issues an official assessment, you have another 45 days to appeal it to the Georgia Tax Court or the appropriate superior court.


You can't skip the protest step and take a proposed assessment straight to court, and a superior court appeal requires a surety bond for the amount in dispute.

## Georgia sales tax FAQs


**What is the sales tax rate in Georgia?** The statewide sales tax rate is 4%, plus local rates of 2% to 5% depending on the county and city. Combined, most areas land between 6% and 9%, with about three dozen jurisdictions at the 9% top end.


**What is the economic nexus threshold in Georgia?**
The threshold is $100,000 in gross revenue or 200 separate transactions delivered into Georgia in the current or previous calendar year. Either one alone is enough to trigger registration.


**Are services taxable in Georgia?**
Mostly no. Professional and personal services are exempt across the board, and Georgia taxes only a short, enumerated list, such as certain in-state transportation and repair or installation services tied to a taxable sale.


**Is SaaS taxable in Georgia?**
Generally not. True cloud-hosted software, where the customer never gets title or possession, is treated as a nontaxable service.


**Are digital products taxable in Georgia?**
Yes, once the buyer gets a permanent right to use the product and the sale isn't tied to continued payments, that product is taxable. Examples include a downloaded movie, song, or e-book.


**Does Georgia charge sales tax on shipping and delivery?**
Yes, Georgia charges sales tax on shipping if the underlying sale is taxable, even if the delivery charge is broken out separately on the invoice.


**Do I need a sales tax permit in Georgia?**
Yes, once you reach the threshold for physical or economic nexus, you must register through the[Georgia Tax Center](https://gtc.dor.ga.gov/) .


**Do marketplace sellers need to collect sales tax in Georgia?**
Sellers do not need to collect taxes on sales for which a marketplace facilitator already collects. However, sellers still need to track those marketplace sales for nexus purposes, and direct sales remain the seller's responsibility.


**How often do businesses need to file sales tax returns in Georgia?**
Monthly, by default. Lower-volume sellers can request quarterly or annual filing once the Department of Revenue signs off based on average tax liability.


**Are groceries and clothing taxable in Georgia?**
Groceries are not charged the 4% state tax but usually are subject to local taxes. Clothing has no exemption at all and is taxed like any other retail good.
